functionalObligations.text: a supplier deposits an ERC-20 into a single shared reserve and receives a transferable claim token one-for-one, and every supplier of that reserve holds the same undifferentiated claim on it
functionalObligations.note: Pl is exact. FLAG FOR STAGE 3: law L2 (Pl implies a claim form plus an exit-liquidity term drawn from Sl, Ad, Bs, Tr, Cv, Wq, Rd, Ps, Sv, Im, Of) is discharged on its first term by Ix and Rb at F2 and is NOT discharged on its second by anything this lane can cite. The corpus discharged it with Im, Sl and Bs; this lane drops all three (Im at F12, Bs and Sl for want of any source read in stage 1 -- the Umbrella/Safety Module contracts were not fetched and stage 1 records Bs as UNCONFIRMED, not confirmed). Aave's real exit guarantee is that a withdrawal reverts when the reserve's available liquidity is short and the rate curve then pays borrowers to repay; that is an incentive, not a mechanism, and no element names it. A resulting INADMISSIBLE verdict is a statement about the evidence base and about L2's term list, not about Aave.

functionalObligations.text: interest is capitalised into a per-reserve index recomputed on every state-changing interaction rather than billed, and the claim token's nominal balance grows with that index so a holder's displayed balance changes without a transfer
functionalObligations.note: Two symbols for one mechanism, and the corpus marker for Rb (FORCED) is retained and sharpened: an aToken is a scaled balance multiplied by the reserve's liquidity index, so Ix is the internal object and Rb is the external presentation of the same object. The vocabulary charges twice and has no way to state that the two symbols denote one thing viewed from two sides. Confirms the corpus residue verbatim.

functionalObligations.text: a borrower designates supplied reserves as collateral and draws an open-ended loan from the same shared reserve, with no maturity and no schedule, recorded as a debt token that accrues by the same index mechanism
functionalObligations.note: setUserUseReserveAsCollateral then borrow then repay. Ft is deliberately NOT emitted: there is no maturity date anywhere in the position, which is the axis on which Aave and Maple differ most and which the vocabulary does record.

functionalObligations.text: solvency is a single scalar computed on chain from the oracle value of each collateral times that asset's liquidation threshold against the oracle value of the debt, and the position is closable when the scalar falls below one
functionalObligations.note: Ct is exact and, contrary to the corpus, first-class rather than derived: the health factor is a named quantity the protocol computes and stores intent against, not something a reader infers from other elements. The per-asset liquidation threshold and LTV are separate configuration fields (LIQUIDATION_THRESHOLD_MASK, LTV_MASK, both MAX_VALID 65535) at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/main/src/contracts/protocol/libraries/configuration/ReserveConfiguration.sol (accessed 2026-08-04); Ct names the test and not that the test has two thresholds per asset.

functionalObligations.text: a liquid-staking-token feed is wrapped in an adapter that rejects any published value implying growth faster than a governance-set maximum yearly ratio, live example 10.64 per cent for wstETH
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent: 10_64 on the wstETH price cap adapter, with updateLstPriceCaps and updateStablePriceCaps as steward domains. Ex names a feed and Tp names a time-weighted price; neither reaches A PREDICATE ON THE FEED'S DERIVATIVE. This is not oracle freshness validation in the sense of L13 -- the value may be fresh and still rejected -- it is a bound on how fast a truth may move, which is the same shape as the mandate's slot 4 applied to an oracle rather than to an agent. Whether these adapters are attached to every live reserve is UNKNOWN.

functionalObligations.text: a third party may repay part of a borrower's debt and seize the borrower's collateral at a bonus, in one permissionless transaction, with no authorisation and no queue
functionalObligations.note: Li is exact here and this is the lane's positive control for it: the clause 'third parties paid to close positions' is true in both halves, which it is not at Maple (see maple.json F13). The per-asset LIQUIDATION_BONUS_MASK is a configuration field (ReserveConfiguration.sol, accessed 2026-08-04); Li names the incentive and not that its size is a governed per-asset parameter.

functionalObligations.text: how much of a position one liquidation may take is itself a computed quantity: at most half the debt when the health factor is above 0.95 and both the collateral and the debt exceed 2000 units of base currency, otherwise all of it, and in no case may the call leave less than 1000 base units of either side standing
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and it re-sites a corpus residue. DEFAULT_LIQUIDATION_CLOSE_FACTOR = 0.5e4, CLOSE_FACTOR_HF_THRESHOLD = 0.95e18, MIN_BASE_MAX_CLOSE_FACTOR_THRESHOLD = 2000e8, MIN_LEFTOVER_BASE = that over two. The corpus files 'no element for the close factor' under JustLend with the gloss 'every Compound descendant has it', which implies Aave has none. Aave has one and a more elaborate one: JustLend's is a constant inside [5 per cent, 90 per cent] while Aave's is a FUNCTION OF HOW UNDERWATER THE POSITION IS AND OF ITS SIZE. Two distinct residues live in this one obligation: (a) a liquidation allowance with its own state, which Li treats as unbounded; (b) a dust floor, which is a constraint on the SHAPE of a permitted partial close and not on the incentive to perform it. The gap is category-wide with two shapes, not JustLend-specific.

functionalObligations.text: the protocol withholds a fraction of borrower interest from suppliers and diverts a further share of the liquidator's bonus, both accruing to a treasury address
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE-REGISTER (Fd), retained from the corpus and extended. The reserve factor appears in the strategy's own output as liquidityRate = borrowRate * U_s * (1 - reserveFactor); RESERVE_FACTOR_MASK and LIQUIDATION_PROTOCOL_FEE_MASK (MAX_VALID 65535 each) are both live per-reserve fields at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/main/src/contracts/protocol/libraries/configuration/ReserveConfiguration.sol (accessed 2026-08-04). DEPARTURE from the corpus, which files the liquidation protocol fee as residue: Fd does reach 'a share of a flow is routed to the protocol'. What Fd does not reach is that this particular share is CARVED OUT OF A THIRD PARTY'S INCENTIVE, so raising it weakens the liquidation guarantee -- a fee that is also a risk parameter. That much remains residue.

functionalObligations.text: anyone may borrow any amount of an enabled reserve with no collateral provided it is returned inside the same transaction
functionalObligations.note: Fl is exact. The facility is per-reserve switchable: FLASHLOAN_ENABLED_MASK at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/main/src/contracts/protocol/libraries/configuration/ReserveConfiguration.sol (accessed 2026-08-04). Conditional prohibition X2 (Fl present with a manipulable pool price and Pl) is armed by construction; Aave prices from Ex rather than from a pool invariant, so the antecedent's second conjunct is not met inside this application.

functionalObligations.text: borrowing power is raised above the ordinary per-asset limits when the collateral and the debt belong to one governance-declared category of assets expected to track each other
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, confirming the corpus. setUserEMode is a user-facing Pool function (https://aave.com/docs/developers/smart-contracts/pool, accessed 2026-08-04) and updateEModeCategories is one of the steward's enumerated domains. No element names correlated-asset margin relief. Note what it is structurally: a SECOND Ct with different constants selected by a declared equivalence class over assets, and the vocabulary has one Ct with no notion of a regime.

functionalObligations.text: each reserve carries a supply cap and a borrow cap that bound aggregate exposure to the asset independently of whether any individual position is solvent
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, confirming the corpus. SUPPLY_CAP_MASK and BORROW_CAP_MASK, both MAX_VALID 68719476735; updateCaps is a steward domain. A cap is a bound on a POPULATION and Ct is a test on an INDIVIDUAL, so no composition of Ct instances yields it. NEW DELTA, and it removes an element the corpus carries: the same bitmap contains NO debt-ceiling field, and its own comment records 'an unoccupied hole of 40 bits from 212 to 251 left from pre 3.7 debtCeiling'. Isolation mode's debt ceiling has been removed from the reserve configuration in the current main tree. The corpus assigns Aave Im with the marker 'FORCED ... the position stays inside the one shared pool'; on this evidence Im is not merely forced but unsupported, and it is DROPPED from the construction. Stage 3 should re-check against a pinned SHA before the paper repeats it.

functionalObligations.text: the borrow rate is a memoryless two-slope function of the reserve's current utilisation alone -- base rate, a first slope up to a kink, a steeper second slope beyond it -- and the supply rate is that borrow rate scaled by supply utilisation and by one minus the reserve factor
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and it is FINDING 1's first row. THE FUNCTIONAL FORM. Ix says an index accrues and is silent on the rate at which it accrues, which is the product. Note the property that distinguishes this row from Morpho's: the rate is a pure function of the CURRENT state, with no memory. A construction that names Ix at Aave and Ix at Morpho asserts they price credit the same way, and they do not -- one is a function, the other a controller (morpho.json F11).

functionalObligations.text: those rate parameters live in a mutable per-reserve struct that only the pool configurator may write, and the configurator's own callers are addresses enumerated in an on-chain role registry that a default admin may add to and remove from
functionalObligations.note: FINDING 1: THE SETTER LOCUS -- a mutable parameter inside the protocol. Aw is APPROXIMATE and this lane emits it uniformly for address-keyed administrative gates, following the corpus's own FORCED use of Aw for role structure at Morpho and the 06-yield lane's use of it for mandate slot 1. DEPARTURE: the corpus does not carry Aw for Aave. What Aw names: the call is gated by address and the gate is mutable (POOL_ADMIN_ROLE, RISK_ADMIN_ROLE, EMERGENCY_ADMIN_ROLE, FLASH_BORROWER_ROLE, BRIDGE_ROLE, ASSET_LISTING_ADMIN_ROLE over OpenZeppelin AccessControl, with add/remove per role and setRoleAdmin under onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE)). What Aw does not name: that the gated thing is a DISCRETIONARY ECONOMIC AUTHORITY rather than a right to participate; and who holds each role, or how many of them there are, which stage 1 records as UNKNOWN for all five targets and the 07-bridges lane records as the party-sort gap. An architectural fact the corpus record predates: earlier Aave V3 deployed one strategy contract per reserve with immutable parameters, so this locus is itself a design that changed.

functionalObligations.text: whatever curve is written must satisfy hard bounds checked at write time: the sum of base rate and both slopes may not exceed 1000 per cent, the kink must lie between 1 and 99 per cent, and the first slope may never exceed the second
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE BOUND. MAX_BORROW_RATE = 1000_00 bps, MIN_OPTIMAL_POINT = 1_00, MAX_OPTIMAL_POINT = 99_00, and the shape constraint variableRateSlope1 <= variableRateSlope2 which forbids a concave curve, all as requires in _setInterestRateParams. The corpus records Aave's rate model as residue but does not record that the rate is a BOUNDED parameter, and the bounding is the same structure as F17. Nothing in the vocabulary states 'this parameter has a permitted interval'.

functionalObligations.text: inside the strategy contract a permitted caller moves the entire curve in one transaction: there is no delay before the change takes effect and no limit on how far it may move
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. FINDING 1: THE LATENCY, at the core layer. Tg is the wrong symbol: nothing here is delayed. The delay and the step limit exist one layer up and in a different repository (F16 to F20), which is why a lane reading only aave-v3-origin would conclude Aave's rate is unbounded in time, and a lane reading only aave-v3-risk-stewards would conclude it is bounded. Both are true of different callers, and the vocabulary cannot hold two authorities over one parameter.

functionalObligations.text: a single named address, held immutably by the contract, may change risk parameters directly without a governance vote
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent). Aw APPROXIMATE, same reading as F13. address public immutable RISK_COUNCIL with modifier onlyRiskCouncil reverting InvalidCaller. Two things Aw does not carry and neither does anything else. (a) THE AGENT MAY BE AN AUTOMATON: AaveStewardInjectorRates, ...Caps, ...EMode and ...DiscountRate read a recommendation from RiskOracle.sol and inject it inside the same envelope under Chainlink or Gelato automation (https://api.github.com/repos/aave-dao/aave-v3-risk-stewards/git/trees/main?recursive=1, accessed 2026-08-04), so 'named agent' must admit a machine acting on an oracle's advice. (b) MANDATE SLOT 6 (agent stake): EMPTY. The Risk Council posts no bond and is not paid by this contract; its only sanction is F20. Contrast Maple (maple.json F19), where the slot is filled and the cross-lane phrase 'accountable only reputationally' is refuted in code.

functionalObligations.text: that address may act only within an enumerated set of parameter families -- caps, rates, the collateral side, e-mode categories, and three kinds of oracle price cap -- and any individual asset or e-mode may be fenced out of its reach entirely
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 (domain whitelist). RESIDUE. Three layers, all in code: (a) the only entry points that exist are updateCaps, updateRates, updateCollateralSide, updateEModeCategories, updateLstPriceCaps, updateStablePriceCaps and updatePendleDiscountRates; (b) _restrictedAddresses[asset] reverts AssetIsRestricted and _restrictedEModes[id] reverts EModeIsRestricted, both written onlyOwner; (c) the EdgeRiskStewardRates, ...Caps, ...EMode and ...DiscountRate variants exist so that a deployment can expose exactly one domain. No element restricts a delegated decision to a domain. Aw is deliberately NOT re-used here: an enumerated set of PERMITTED ACTIONS over PERMITTED SUBJECTS is not an identity gate, and stretching Aw across both would erase the distinction between who may act and what they may touch.

functionalObligations.text: each parameter carries its own maximum change per update, expressed either as a percentage of the current value or as an absolute step, and an update outside that range reverts
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 3 (magnitude cap). RESIDUE. struct RiskParamConfig { uint40 minDelay; uint256 maxPercentChange; }, checked by _updateWithinAllowedRange with an isChangeRelative flag, with separate configs per family (Config{CollateralConfig, EmodeConfig, RateConfig, CapConfig, PriceCapConfig}). Ct is a solvency test, not a parameter envelope; no element expresses a numeric domain restriction on a delegated decision.

functionalObligations.text: no parameter may be moved again until a minimum interval has passed since that same parameter was last moved on that same asset, each pair carrying its own timestamp
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 4 (rate-of-change limit or delay). RESIDUE. riskConfig.minDelay checked against a per-(asset, parameter) lastUpdated -- the contract keeps supplyCapLastUpdated, borrowCapLastUpdated, optimalUsageRatioLastUpdated, baseVariableRateLastUpdated, variableRateSlope1LastUpdated, variableRateSlope2LastUpdated, ltvLastUpdated, liquidationThresholdLastUpdated, liquidationBonusLastUpdated and e-mode equivalents. THE MECHANISM IS A DEBOUNCE AND Tg IS THE WRONG SYMBOL: this is a cooldown SINCE the last change, not a delay BEFORE execution, and the steward's own change is immediate. This is one of four distinct mechanisms occupying this slot across the lane -- debounce here, queue-and-accept timelock at MetaMorpho, one-sided cooldown at Spark's CapAutomator, continuously refilling token bucket at Spark's ALM. A formalism with one field called 'rate-of-change limit' conflates a limit on HOW OFTEN with a limit on HOW MUCH PER UNIT TIME.

functionalObligations.text: the principal may zero the envelope or fence any asset at any time, but cannot remove the agent: the agent's address is fixed at deployment and this contract holds no way to change it
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 (revocation). RESIDUE, and it is the sharpest of the five parts here. setRiskConfig, setAddressRestricted and setEModeCategoryRestricted are all onlyOwner (the governance executor), so the owner can reduce the mandate to nothing without touching the council; but RISK_COUNCIL is immutable, so WHAT IS REVOCABLE IS THE MANDATE'S CONTENTS AND NOT ITS HOLDER. Revoking the agent means retiring the whole steward instance (or removing its role at the ACLManager, F13) -- a different act at a different contract. Aw is NOT emitted: a mutable membership set is not the claim 'a principal may withdraw a delegated economic authority', and here the membership is not even mutable. Across the corpus stage 4 has counted ZERO revocation obligations; this is one of five added by this lane.

functionalObligations.text: any reserve may be frozen or paused individually, and a distinct emergency role exists whose purpose is to do so
functionalObligations.note: Gp is supported. ACTIVE_MASK, FROZEN_MASK and PAUSED_MASK are per-reserve configuration bits, and EMERGENCY_ADMIN_ROLE is a declared role at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aave-dao/aave-v3-origin/main/src/contracts/protocol/configuration/ACLManager.sol (accessed 2026-08-04). Gp names one halt; it does not name that there are THREE graduated states here (active, frozen -- no new positions but existing ones may be closed -- and paused), which is a lattice of degrees of stop and reads as a single boolean. Who holds the role is UNKNOWN.

functionalObligations.text: the pool and its configurator sit behind admin-upgradeable proxies whose implementations may be replaced by an owner the source names as the governance
functionalObligations.note: Up is exact. setPoolImpl, setPoolConfiguratorImpl, setAddressAsProxy and _updateImpl, all external override onlyOwner over Ownable, deploying InitializableImmutableAdminUpgradeabilityProxy; the contract's own comment reads 'Owned by the Aave Governance'. Law L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is discharged by F23, subject to the caveat there. Prohibition X9 (Up with immediate single-key control) is NOT armed on this evidence and is not disarmed either: the owner's identity and quorum are UNKNOWN, which is exactly the 07-bridges lane's finding that the risk is a property of the holder and the vocabulary has no party sort.

functionalObligations.text: a governance action arrives as a payload bridged from a separate governance chain, is queued on receipt, becomes executable by anyone only after a per-executor delay of between one and ten days, and expires if left unexecuted through a grace period
functionalObligations.note: Tg and Xm both supported, and both were carried by the corpus without a source; this lane supplies one. MIN_EXECUTION_DELAY 1 day, MAX_EXECUTION_DELAY 10 days, EXPIRATION_DELAY 35 days, GRACE_PERIOD 7 days; executionTime = payload.queuedAt + payload.delay and executePayload has no caller restriction beyond state validation. Xm is warranted by the payload arriving from the governance chain, not by any user asset movement -- so Aave's cross-domain element is a CONTROL-PLANE object, which the vocabulary places in the same group as bridged value and cannot distinguish. Two things Tg does not say and both matter here: that the delay is per-executor and configurable, and that it protects only THIS path -- the steward (F16 to F20) reaches the same parameters with no delay at all.

paper.title: Aave V3
paper.label: cat:lnd:aave
paper.blurb: A supplier deposits a fungible token into one shared reserve and receives a transferable claim token whose nominal balance grows as the reserve's index accrues. A borrower marks supplied reserves as collateral and draws an open-ended loan from the same reserve, with no maturity and no schedule, recorded as a debt token accruing by that same index. The price of the loan is a memoryless two-slope function of the reserve's current utilisation, held in a mutable per-reserve struct that only the pool configurator may write, and bounded at write time on its level, on where its kink may sit and on its shape. Solvency is a single scalar computed on chain from the oracle value of each collateral against the oracle value of the debt. A borrower closes by repaying; anyone else closes by repaying part of the debt and seizing collateral at a bonus, and how much of a position one liquidation may take is itself a computed quantity, falling out of how far underwater the position is and how large it is.
paper.witnessReason: The element-set decomposition records $Bs$, $Cd$, $Em$, $Im$ and $Sl$; the witness carries none of them and adds $Aw$. $Im$ goes because the reserve configuration in the current tree holds no debt-ceiling field at all --- the bitmap's own comment records the unoccupied bits left where one used to sit --- so the fenced market the corpus called forced is not merely forced but unsupported, and the same drop follows downstream at the protocol that forked this one. $Bs$ and $Sl$ go because the Safety Module contracts were not read and this lane carries no element on memory; $Cd$ and $Em$ go for the same reason; $Aw$ arrives for the address-keyed administrative gate through which every parameter this protocol has is written. That leaves the exit-liquidity term of the pooled-claim law open where the corpus closed it, and the choice is deliberate rather than an omission: what actually guarantees a supplier's exit here is that a withdrawal reverts when the reserve is short and the curve then pays borrowers to repay, which is an incentive and not one of the mechanisms the term offers.
paper.residueNote: The residue here is the entire surface a risk team manages. What the vocabulary keeps is that money is pooled, that an index accrues, that a test is run, and that someone is paid to close a failing position; what it loses is every quantity those mechanisms are actually set to --- the shape of the rate curve and the interval its parameters must lie in, the allowance one liquidation may take and the remainder it may not leave, the caps that bound an asset's whole population rather than any individual position, and the permitted drift of a price feed. The sharpest instance is the steward: a named address, fixed at deployment, may move rates, caps, collateral parameters, correlated-asset categories and oracle growth limits with no vote, and of that mandate the decomposition names only the agent, and names it only by stretching an address-keyed permission gate. The enumerated domains it may touch, the maximum step per update, the minimum interval before the same parameter of the same asset may move again, and the principal's power to empty the envelope while being unable to remove the agent are all residue --- and across every instance of this shape in the category the domain, the magnitude cap and the revocation are residue without exception. Here the parts are not merely present but factored into one reusable validator, and that validator bounds the rate through the same code that bounds the caps, which is why the price of credit and the delegated mandate are one gap stated twice rather than two gaps.
